claim: Transcription often occurs in bursts as gene promoters switch stochastically between active and inactive states.
source: Transcription often occurs in bursts as gene promoters switch stochastically between active and inactive states.
evidence: This is a general statement about transcriptional bursting that draws from established scientific understanding in the field.

claim: Enhancers can dictate transcriptional activity in animal development through the modulation of burst frequency, duration, or amplitude.
source: Enhancers can dictate transcriptional activity in animal development through the modulation of burst frequency, duration, or amplitude.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about how enhancers regulate transcription.

claim: All even-skipped enhancers increase transcription by upregulating burst frequency and amplitude while burst duration remains largely constant.
source: For example, in Berrocal et al., 2020, we showed that despite responding to different transcription factors, all even-skipped enhancers increase transcription by upregulating burst frequency and amplitude while burst duration remains largely constant.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: Bursting strategies remain consistent in endogenous and ectopic even-skipped expression.
source: Here, we generated ectopic even-skipped transcription patterns in fruit fly embryos and discovered that bursting strategies remain consistent in endogenous and ectopic even-skipped expression.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study based on experimental data.

claim: The results provide evidence for a unified molecular mechanism shaping even-skipped bursting strategies.
source: These results provide evidence for a unified molecular mechanism shaping even-skipped bursting strategies and serve as a starting point to uncover the realm of strategies employed by other enhancers.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Enhancers are cis-regulatory elements that can act at a distance to modulate the transcription of genes.
source: In animal development, enhancers, cis-regulatory elements that can act at a distance to modulate the transcription of genes (Banerji et al., 1981; Banerji et al., 1983; Gillies et al., 1983) orchestrate the formation of gene expression patterns that dictate animal body plans (Davidson, 2010; Roberta, 2015; Lewis, 1978).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to foundational work on enhancers.

claim: Enhancers orchestrate the formation of gene expression patterns that dictate animal body plans.
source: In animal development, enhancers, cis-regulatory elements that can act at a distance to modulate the transcription of genes (Banerji et al., 1981; Banerji et al., 1983; Gillies et al., 1983) orchestrate the formation of gene expression patterns that dictate animal body plans (Davidson, 2010; Roberta, 2015; Lewis, 1978).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Transcription of most genes occurs in stochastic pulses, or bursts, of mRNA synthesis.
source: At the single-cell level, transcription of most genes has been shown to occur in stochastic pulses, or bursts, of mRNA synthesis (Dar et al., 2012; Golding et al., 2005; McKnight and Miller, 1979; Raj et al., 2006; Senecal et al., 2014; Skupsky et al., 2010; Zenklusen et al., 2008), and patterned developmental genes are no exception (Berrocal et al., 2020; Bothma et al., 2014; Fukaya et al., 2016; Lammers et al., 2020; Zoller et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Patterned developmental genes exhibit transcriptional bursting.
source: At the single-cell level, transcription of most genes has been shown to occur in stochastic pulses, or bursts, of mRNA synthesis (Dar et al., 2012; Golding et al., 2005; McKnight and Miller, 1979; Raj et al., 2006; Senecal et al., 2014; Skupsky et al., 2010; Zenklusen et al., 2008), and patterned developmental genes are no exception (Berrocal et al., 2020; Bothma et al., 2014; Fukaya et al., 2016; Lammers et al., 2020; Zoller et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on developmental genes.

claim: Enhancers can read out transcription factor concentration and modulate transcriptional bursting dynamics through binding sites for transcription factors.
source: Enhancers typically feature binding sites for several transcription factors proteins. Through these binding sites, enhancers can read out transcription factor concentration and modulate transcriptional bursting dynamics of the genes they regulate (Bothma et al., 2014; Bothma et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2018; Fukaya et al., 2016; Small et al., 1992; Yuh et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the two-state model of promoter activity, bursts result from a gene promoter that switches stochastically between an inactive state (OFF) and an active state (ON) at a rate kon.
source: Transcriptional bursting can be described by the two-state model of promoter activity (Lionnet and Singer, 2012; Peccoud and Ycart, 1995; Sanchez et al., 2013) that depicts bursts as the result of a gene promoter that switches stochastically between an inactive state, OFF, and an active state, ON, at a rate kon.
evidence: This claim describes a theoretical model supported by citations.

claim: When the promoter is in its ON state, it loads RNA Pol II molecules onto the gene at a rate r until the promoter transitions back to the OFF state at a rate koff.
source: When the promoter is in its ON state, it loads RNA Pol II molecules onto the gene at a rate r until, eventually, the promoter transitions back to the OFF state at a rate koff and mRNA synthesis stops (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This claim describes the two-state model and references Figure 1A and B for visual support.

claim: The five enhancers that form the seven stripes of even-skipped expression in Drosophila melanogaster employ the same kinetic strategy to control the rate of mRNA synthesis by modulating burst frequency and amplitude while leaving burst duration largely unchanged.
source: For example, using live-imaging and statistical modeling, we previously showed that the five enhancers that form the seven stripes of even-skipped (eve) expression in Drosophila melanogaster, despite each interacting with a different set of transcription factors, employ the same kinetic strategy to control the rate of mRNA synthesis: they modulate burst frequency and amplitude, while leaving burst duration largely unchanged (Berrocal et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: The transcriptional control of various D. melanogaster gap genes is characterized by the shared modulation of burst frequency and duration, while burst amplitude remains constant.
source: Similarly, another study employing single-molecule mRNA FISH suggested that the transcriptional control of various D. melanogaster gap genes is characterized by the shared modulation of burst frequency and duration, while burst amplitude remains constant (Zoller et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to another study.

claim: Wild-type eve stripe 2 is expressed through the interplay of the activators Bicoid and Hunchback with the repressors Giant and Krüppel.
source: eve stripes result from the interplay of various activators and repressors, for instance, wild-type eve stripe 2 is expressed through the interplay of the activators Bicoid and Hunchback with the repressors Giant and Krüppel. The latter define the anterior and posterior boundaries of eve stripe 2, respectively.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about eve stripe 2 regulation, as indicated by the reference to Figure 1C and D being based on Levine, 2013 and Peel et al., 2005.

claim: Giant and Krüppel define the anterior and posterior boundaries of eve stripe 2, respectively.
source: eve stripes result from the interplay of various activators and repressors, for instance, wild-type eve stripe 2 is expressed through the interplay of the activators Bicoid and Hunchback with the repressors Giant and Krüppel. The latter define the anterior and posterior boundaries of eve stripe 2, respectively.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about eve stripe 2 regulation.

claim: The eveMS2-BAC reporter system carries an ~20 kb DNA fragment around the D. melanogaster eve coding region containing the five eve enhancers responsible for regulating the expression of the seven eve stripes.
source: As our starting point, we took a previously established BAC-based eve-MS2 reporter system (Berrocal et al., 2020) that carries an ~20 kb DNA fragment around the D. melanogaster eve coding region containing the five eve enhancers responsible for regulating the expression of the seven eve stripes, other cis-regulatory elements such as neuronal and muscular regulatory elements (Fujioka et al., 1999; Fujioka et al., 2013) that might influence eve stripe expression in early development (Fujioka et al., 1999; Fujioka et al., 2013), and the late element (LE) that upregulates eve expression in all stripes in response to the EVE protein (Fujioka et al., 1996; Jiang et al., 1991; Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental construct used in the study, supported by citations and reference to Figure 2A.

claim: The MS2 reporter system fluorescently labels nascent mRNA molecules resulting in sites of nascent transcription appearing as puncta whose fluorescence is proportional to the number of active RNA Pol II molecules.
source: The MS2 reporter system fluorescently labels nascent mRNA molecules resulting in sites of nascent transcription appearing as puncta whose fluorescence is proportional to the number of active RNA Pol II molecules.
evidence: This describes the technical principle of the MS2 system, which is established knowledge in the field.

claim: The MS2 system allows for the visualization of transcriptional bursting at single locus resolution, in real-time, in living embryos.
source: As a result, the system allows for the visualization of transcriptional bursting at single locus resolution, in real-time, in living embryos (Chubb et al., 2006; Ferguson and Larson, 2013; Garcia et al., 2013; Golding et al., 2005; Golding and Cox, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies using the MS2 system.

claim: When inserted into the D. melanogaster genome, eveMS2-BAC expresses in seven stripes that recapitulate the wild-type expression of eve.
source: When inserted into the D. melanogaster genome, eveMS2-BAC expresses in seven stripes that recapitulate the wild-type expression of eve (Figure 2B; Berrocal et al., 2020) as observed by FISH and live-imaging experiments (Lammers et al., 2020; Lim et al., 2018; Luengo Hendriks et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and reference to Figure 2B showing the expression pattern.

claim: The anterior boundary of eve stripe 2 is established through repression by Giant.
source: To make this possible, we leveraged the fact that the anterior boundary of eve stripe 2 is established through repression by Giant (Small et al., 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Small et al., 1992.

claim: Deleting three Giant binding sites within the minimal regulatory element of the eve stripe 2 enhancer produces a strong anterior expansion of eve stripe 2 in the context of a reporter driven by eveS2-MRE.
source: Classic work by Small et al. identified a minimal regulatory element of the eve stripe 2 enhancer (eveS2-MRE; Figure 2A) and found that deleting three Giant binding sites within this minimal enhancer produced a strong anterior expansion of eve stripe 2 in the context of a reporter driven by eveS2-MRE (Small et al., 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Small et al., 1992 and reference to Figure 2A.

claim: eveS1wt-eveS2Gt- embryos showed only transient ectopic expression at the inter-stripe region between eve stripes 1 and 2.
source: Live imaging experiments on eveS1wt-eveS2Gt- embryos showed only transient ectopic expression at the inter-stripe region between eve stripes 1 and 2.
evidence: This is an observation from the live imaging experiments conducted in this study.

claim: Transient inter-stripe expression in eveS1wt-eveS2Gt- embryos lasts until 30–35 min into nc14.
source: This transient inter-stripe expression lasts until 30–35 min into nc14; while inter-stripe expression between eve stripe 1 and eve stripe 2 disappears after ~20 min in wild-type embryos (compare Figure 2B and C; compare Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is based on data from live imaging experiments and comparison of figures.

claim: Inter-stripe expression between eve stripe 1 and eve stripe 2 disappears after ~20 min in wild-type embryos.
source: This transient inter-stripe expression lasts until 30–35 min into nc14; while inter-stripe expression between eve stripe 1 and eve stripe 2 disappears after ~20 min in wild-type embryos (compare Figure 2B and C; compare Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is based on data from live imaging experiments and comparison of figures.

claim: eveS1wt-eveS2Gt- embryos did not produce the robust anterior expansion of eve stripe 2 described for the eveS2-MRE alone.
source: These eveS1wt-eveS2Gt- embryos did not produce the robust anterior expansion of eve stripe 2 described for the eveS2-MRE alone (Small et al., 1992).
evidence: This is an observation from the current study compared to previous work.

claim: The muted anterior expansion in eveS1wt-eveS2Gt- embryos is attributed to regulatory sequences not present in the original minimal eve stripe 2 reporter construct which might provide a buffering effect to the disruption of the three Giant binding sites.
source: We attribute this muted anterior expansion in eveS1wt-eveS2Gt- embryos (Figure 2C) to the regulatory sequences not present in the original minimal eve stripe 2 reporter construct which might provide a buffering effect to the disruption of the three Giant binding sites (López-Rivera et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results with support from a citation.

claim: eveS1∆-eveS2wt embryos exhibited a dim eve stripe 1 (~30% of embryo length) after ~30 min into nc14.
source: Unexpectedly, these embryos still exhibited a dim eve stripe 1 (~30% of embryo length) after ~30 min into nc14, perhaps due to the activity of the eve late element; and a dim additional anterior stripe that we refer to as eve stripe 0 (~20% embryo length) after ~25 min into nc14.
evidence: This is an observation from the live imaging experiments.

claim: The dim eve stripe 1 in eveS1∆-eveS2wt embryos is perhaps due to the activity of the eve late element.
source: Unexpectedly, these embryos still exhibited a dim eve stripe 1 (~30% of embryo length) after ~30 min into nc14, perhaps due to the activity of the eve late element; and a dim additional anterior stripe that we refer to as eve stripe 0 (~20% embryo length) after ~25 min into nc14.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed data.

claim: eveS1∆-eveS2wt embryos exhibited a dim additional anterior stripe referred to as eve stripe 0 (~20% embryo length) after ~25 min into nc14.
source: Unexpectedly, these embryos still exhibited a dim eve stripe 1 (~30% of embryo length) after ~30 min into nc14, perhaps due to the activity of the eve late element; and a dim additional anterior stripe that we refer to as eve stripe 0 (~20% embryo length) after ~25 min into nc14.
evidence: This is an observation from the live imaging experiments.

claim: Small et al., 1992 identified a 'head patch' of gene expression when assaying the regulation of the minimal regulatory element of the eve stripe 2 enhancer.
source: In a previous study, Small et al., 1992 identified a 'head patch' of gene expression when assaying the regulation of the minimal regulatory element of the eve stripe 2 enhancer.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Small et al., 1992.

claim: The appearance of eve stripe 0 indicates a repressive role of eve stripe 1 enhancer beyond the anterior boundary of eve stripe 1.
source: Thus, the appearance of eve stripe 0 indicates a repressive role of eve stripe 1 enhancer beyond the anterior boundary of eve stripe 1 (Figure 2D), and it may imply that the minimal regulatory element of the eve stripe 2 enhancer can indeed drive expression in this head patch when eve stripe 1 enhancer is not present.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The minimal regulatory element of the eve stripe 2 enhancer can drive expression in the head patch when eve stripe 1 enhancer is not present.
source: Thus, the appearance of eve stripe 0 indicates a repressive role of eve stripe 1 enhancer beyond the anterior boundary of eve stripe 1 (Figure 2D), and it may imply that the minimal regulatory element of the eve stripe 2 enhancer can indeed drive expression in this head patch when eve stripe 1 enhancer is not present.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos exhibited a stronger and longer-lasting inter-stripe expression between eve stripe 1 and eve stripe 2 than observed in eveS1wt-eveS2Gt-.
source: Surprisingly, eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos revealed large ectopic regions of eve expression more complex than the sum of patterns displayed by the independent mutants described above. Beyond a stronger and longer-lasting inter-stripe expression between eve stripe 1 and eve stripe 2 than observed in eveS1wt-eveS2Gt-, eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos exhibited the following notable features: a stronger-than-wild-type eve stripe 2 (located at ~40% of embryo length); the presence of eve stripe 1 (~30% of embryo length) and eve stripe 0 (~20% embryo length); and many eve-active nuclei in normally silent inter-stripe regions between eve stripe 2 and eve stripe 0 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is an observation from the live imaging experiments.

claim: eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos exhibited a stronger-than-wild-type eve stripe 2 located at ~40% of embryo length.
source: Surprisingly, eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos revealed large ectopic regions of eve expression more complex than the sum of patterns displayed by the independent mutants described above. Beyond a stronger and longer-lasting inter-stripe expression between eve stripe 1 and eve stripe 2 than observed in eveS1wt-eveS2Gt-, eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos exhibited the following notable features: a stronger-than-wild-type eve stripe 2 (located at ~40% of embryo length); the presence of eve stripe 1 (~30% of embryo length) and eve stripe 0 (~20% embryo length); and many eve-active nuclei in normally silent inter-stripe regions between eve stripe 2 and eve stripe 0 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is an observation from the live imaging experiments.

claim: eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos exhibited the presence of eve stripe 1 (~30% of embryo length) and eve stripe 0 (~20% embryo length).
source: Surprisingly, eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos revealed large ectopic regions of eve expression more complex than the sum of patterns displayed by the independent mutants described above. Beyond a stronger and longer-lasting inter-stripe expression between eve stripe 1 and eve stripe 2 than observed in eveS1wt-eveS2Gt-, eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos exhibited the following notable features: a stronger-than-wild-type eve stripe 2 (located at ~40% of embryo length); the presence of eve stripe 1 (~30% of embryo length) and eve stripe 0 (~20% embryo length); and many eve-active nuclei in normally silent inter-stripe regions between eve stripe 2 and eve stripe 0 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is an observation from the live imaging experiments.

claim: eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos exhibited many eve-active nuclei in normally silent inter-stripe regions between eve stripe 2 and eve stripe 0.
source: Surprisingly, eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos revealed large ectopic regions of eve expression more complex than the sum of patterns displayed by the independent mutants described above. Beyond a stronger and longer-lasting inter-stripe expression between eve stripe 1 and eve stripe 2 than observed in eveS1wt-eveS2Gt-, eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos exhibited the following notable features: a stronger-than-wild-type eve stripe 2 (located at ~40% of embryo length); the presence of eve stripe 1 (~30% of embryo length) and eve stripe 0 (~20% embryo length); and many eve-active nuclei in normally silent inter-stripe regions between eve stripe 2 and eve stripe 0 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is an observation from the live imaging experiments.

claim: The knock-out of eve stripe 1 enhancer coupled with the disruption of Gt-binding sites in eve stripe 2 enhancer renders more ectopic expression on the anterior half of fruit fly embryos than the independent disruptions in eveS1∆-eveS2wt and eveS1wt-eveS2Gt-.
source: The fact that the knock-out of eve stripe 1 enhancer coupled with the disruption of Gt-binding sites in eve stripe 2 enhancer renders more ectopic expression on the anterior half of fruit fly embryos than the independent disruptions in eveS1∆-eveS2wt and eveS1wt-eveS2Gt- implies that the repressive activity of the eve stripe 1 enhancer synergizes with the repression exerted by Giant—and potentially with other unidentified transcription factors that bind in the vicinity of Gt-binding sites—on the eve stripe 2 enhancer.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the different mutant phenotypes.

claim: The repressive activity of the eve stripe 1 enhancer synergizes with the repression exerted by Giant on the eve stripe 2 enhancer.
source: The fact that the knock-out of eve stripe 1 enhancer coupled with the disruption of Gt-binding sites in eve stripe 2 enhancer renders more ectopic expression on the anterior half of fruit fly embryos than the independent disruptions in eveS1∆-eveS2wt and eveS1wt-eveS2Gt- implies that the repressive activity of the eve stripe 1 enhancer synergizes with the repression exerted by Giant—and potentially with other unidentified transcription factors that bind in the vicinity of Gt-binding sites—on the eve stripe 2 enhancer.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Gt binding sites in eve stripe 2 enhancer may recognize other transcription factors besides Giant.
source: The hypothesis that Gt binding sites in eve stripe 2 enhancer may recognize other transcription factors was proposed by Small et al., 1992, who observed that the anterior expansion of eve stripe 2 that results from disrupting Gt-binding sites in eve stripe 2 enhancer is 'somewhat more severe' than the expansion observed in Gt- embryos.
evidence: This hypothesis is supported by citation to Small et al., 1992.

claim: The eve stripe 1 enhancer plays a repressing role in the anterior half of fruit fly embryos which synergizes with the Giant repressor and likely with other transcriptional regulators bound to Gt binding sites or their vicinity in the eve stripe 2 enhancer.
source: Taken together, our results suggest that the eve stripe 1 enhancer plays a repressing role in the anterior half of fruit fly embryos which synergizes with the Giant repressor and likely with other transcriptional regulators bound to Gt binding sites or their vicinity in the eve stripe 2 enhancer.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: There is cross-activity between the eve stripe 1 and 2 enhancers that impacts eve expression in the anterior half of the embryo.
source: This argues in favor of cross-activity between the eve stripe 1 and 2 enhancers that impacts eve expression in the anterior half of the embryo.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The eve stripe 1 enhancer might be playing a role in the regulation of eve stripe 2.
source: eve stripe 1 enhancer might be also playing a role in the regulation of eve stripe 2, as Giant-binding site deletions in the eve stripe 2 enhancer alone do not result in the stronger-than-wild-type eve stripe 2 observed in eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the observed data.

claim: Coupling the disruption of Giant-binding sites in the eve stripe 2 enhancer with the deletion of the eve stripe 1 enhancer produces different mutant patterns than the sum of the individual mutants.
source: In summary, coupling the disruption of Giant-binding sites in the eve stripe 2 enhancer with the deletion of the eve stripe 1 enhancer produces different mutant patterns than the sum of the individual mutants.
evidence: This is a summary observation from the experimental data.

claim: Ectopic regions show lower levels of mean MS2 fluorescence than endogenous regions.
source: Overall, ectopic regions show lower levels of mean MS2 fluorescence than endogenous regions, as is evident by comparing eve the interstripe 1–2 and eve stripe 0 against eve stripe 1, eve stripe 2, and eve stripe 3 in eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos (Figure 2E, Right).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Lower MS2 fluorescence in ectopic regions is perhaps due to the unavailability of optimal concentrations of transcription factors.
source: This is perhaps due to the unavailability of optimal concentrations of transcription factors; for example a lack of activators or an excess of repressors with respect to the concentrations found in endogenous regions (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed data.

claim: Nuclei in all wild-type stripes achieve higher levels of transcription by upregulating average bursting frequency (kon) and amplitude (r), while average burst duration (koff–1) remains largely the same.
source: Consistent with our previous work (Berrocal et al., 2020), we find that endogenous stripes in eveMS2-BAC wild-type embryos modulate their transcriptional output (mean MS2 fluorescence in wild-type embryos ranges from 2 to 15 AU) by tuning the average kon (from 0.5 to 1.5 OFF to ON promoter transitions per minute) and r (from an average fluorescence increase at a rate of 5 AU per minute to 10 AU per minute). The average koff value remains largely constant (0.5 ON to OFF promoter transitions per minute), with only a minor downregulation at high transcription outputs (Figure 3C). Thus, we confirm that eve-active nuclei in all wild-type stripes achieve higher levels of transcription by upregulating average bursting frequency (kon) and amplitude (r), while average burst duration (koff–1) remains largely the same.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study consistent with previous work, supported by data in Figure 3C.

claim: Endogenous stripes in eveS1wt-eveS2Gt- and eveS1∆-eveS2wt embryos followed the same bursting strategy observed in wild-type embryos, regardless of whether stripes were activated by wild-type or mutant enhancers.
source: eveS1wt-eveS2Gt- (Figure 3D) and eveS1∆-eveS2wt (Figure 3E) embryos did not yield enough ectopic nuclei for cpHMM inference. However, their endogenous stripes followed the same bursting strategy observed in wild-type embryos, regardless of whether stripes were activated by wild-type or mutant enhancers (see SI Section: Complementary analysis of bursting parameters in Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by data in Figures 3D and 3E.

claim: Bursting parameters in endogenous and ectopic eve-active nuclei in eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos follow the same trends as wild-type embryos.
source: Despite these differences in transcriptional output, bursting parameters in endogenous and ectopic eve-active nuclei in eveS1∆-eveS2Gt- embryos follow the same trends as wild-type embryos (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: In all regions–both endogenous and ectopic–enhancers increase transcription by increasing kon and r, while koff remains largely constant.
source: In all regions–both endogenous and ectopic–enhancers increase transcription by increasing in kon and r, while koff remains largely constant (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by data in Figure 3F.

claim: All eve enhancers modulate their transcriptional output by increasing burst frequency (kon) and amplitude (r).
source: Taken together, our results show that all eve enhancers modulate their transcriptional output by increasing burst frequency (kon) and amplitude (r).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: koff, which shapes burst duration, remains largely constant, and shows a subtle drop as the mean MS2 fluorescence of nuclei increases.
source: koff, which shapes burst duration, remains largely constant, and shows a subtle drop as the mean MS2 fluorescence of nuclei increases.
evidence: This is a summary observation from the experimental data.

claim: eve strategies of bursting control are robust to mutations on eve enhancers.
source: eve strategies of bursting control are robust to mutations on eve enhancers, and remain consistent in the presence of a myriad of inputs, including ectopic inputs different from those that shape the transcription of the seven canonical eve stripes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: eve strategies of bursting control remain consistent in the presence of a myriad of inputs, including ectopic inputs different from those that shape the transcription of the seven canonical eve stripes.
source: eve strategies of bursting control are robust to mutations on eve enhancers, and remain consistent in the presence of a myriad of inputs, including ectopic inputs different from those that shape the transcription of the seven canonical eve stripes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Drosophila gap genes modulate bursting through an increase in frequency and duration, while burst amplitude remains unchanged.
source: Indeed, (Zoller et al., 2018) observed that Drosophila gap genes, controlled by independent promoters and enhancers, modulate bursting through another common strategy; an increase in frequency and duration, while burst amplitude remains unchanged.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zoller et al., 2018.

claim: Bursting control strategies for gap genes persist despite genetic perturbations.
source: A subsequent study by P.-T. Chen et al., 2023 found further evidence of a tight relationship between burst frequency and duration among gap genes. Consistent with our findings on eve bursting control, the authors observed that bursting control strategies for gap genes persist despite genetic perturbations.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to P.-T. Chen et al., 2023.

claim: Disrupting Dorsal binding sites on the snail minimal distal enhancer leads to a reduction in both the amplitude and duration of transcription bursting in fruit fly embryos.
source: Furthermore, in a recent study, Syed et al., 2023 utilized a Hidden Markov Model to analyze live imaging data of transcription driven by snail enhancers. The study concludes that disrupting Dorsal binding sites on the snail minimal distal enhancer leads to a reduction in both the amplitude and duration of transcription bursting in fruit fly embryos.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Syed et al., 2023.

claim: Topological dynamics of bacterial chromosomes brought by transcriptional activity shape bursting in bacteria.
source: Previous work showed that topological dynamics of bacterial chromosomes brought by transcriptional activity shape bursting in bacteria (Chong et al., 2014); while histone acetylation of the circadian promoter Bmal1 modulates burst frequency in mammalian cells (Nicolas et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Chong et al., 2014.

claim: Histone acetylation of the circadian promoter Bmal1 modulates burst frequency in mammalian cells.
source: Previous work showed that topological dynamics of bacterial chromosomes brought by transcriptional activity shape bursting in bacteria (Chong et al., 2014); while histone acetylation of the circadian promoter Bmal1 modulates burst frequency in mammalian cells (Nicolas et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Nicolas et al., 2018.

claim: The dynamics of RNA Pol I–subunit assembly affect transcriptional output.
source: Furthermore, Gorski et al., 2008 observed that the dynamics of RNA Pol I–subunit assembly affect transcriptional output.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gorski et al., 2008.

claim: The naturally established concentration gradient of Bone Morphogenetic Protein (BMP) defines the bursting frequency of BMP target genes in fruit fly embryos.
source: The importance of modulating the concentration and availability of key transcription factors is emphasized by Hoppe et al., 2020. Their findings show that the naturally established concentration gradient of Bone Morphogenetic Protein (BMP) defines the bursting frequency of BMP target genes in fruit fly embryos.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hoppe et al., 2020.

claim: The transcription factor Knirps represses the activity of the eve stripe 4+6 enhancer by gradually decreasing burst frequency until the locus sets into a fully reversible quiescent state.
source: Another example that underscores the significance of transcription factor availability in shaping bursting strategies was illustrated by Zhao et al., 2024. Using optogenetic LEXY-mediated modulation of nuclear protein export (Niopek et al., 2016) in fruit fly embryos, this study found that the transcription factor Knirps represses the activity of the eve stripe 4+6 enhancer by gradually decreasing burst frequency until the locus sets into a fully reversible quiescent state.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhao et al., 2024.

claim: Core promoter elements, such as the TATA box, the initiator element, and the downstream core promoter element play a fundamental role in shaping transcriptional bursting in genes of D. melanogaster embryos.
source: Recent studies using MS2 live imaging have described a fundamental role of core promoter elements, such as the TATA box, the initiator element, and the downstream core promoter element in shaping transcriptional bursting in genes of D. melanogaster embryos (Pimmett et al., 2021; Yokoshi et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pimmett et al., 2021 and Yokoshi et al., 2022.

claim: A survey of 17 genes in the actin family of the amoeba Dictyostelium discoideum, featuring identical coding sequences but distinct promoters, revealed different bursting behaviors for each gene.
source: Furthermore, a survey of 17 genes in the actin family of the amoeba Dictyostelium discoideum (Tunnacliffe et al., 2018), featuring identical coding sequences but distinct promoters, revealed different bursting behaviors for each gene.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tunnacliffe et al., 2018.

claim: A molecular mechanism coupled to eve transcription restricts the landscape of bursting strategies available to eve enhancers.
source: Both possibilities suggest that a molecular mechanism coupled to eve transcription restricts the landscape of bursting strategies available to eve enhancers.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the discussion of possible mechanisms.

claim: eve bursting strategies are a fundamental property of enhancers and promoters—and not the result of changing trans-regulatory environments.
source: Our results indicate that eve bursting strategies are a fundamental property of enhancers and promoters—and not the result of changing trans-regulatory environments—and show that eve enhancers merely act as knobs, robust to mutations, that tune transcriptional output levels by modulating bursting through a largely fixed koff and shifting r and kon.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.
